text.heading: Three made-up decisions
text.lede: This is an example. The three decisions are made up, about a garden shed. Tap Yes or Not yes. Not yes asks “if not yes, then?” and offers another way, with its own Yes and Not yes. Every card has a box for your own words, and a Yes can carry a condition. At the end, press Copy my answers to see the text you would paste into a chat with your AI. To use it on your own decisions, give your AI the words in the box below.

about: A made-up example. Imagine a garden shed that needs painting before winter.
It is bare timber now. A tin of green paint is already in the garage, so green costs nothing and can start tomorrow.
questions.q: Do you want the shed painted green?
questions.yes: It gets painted green with the tin in the garage.
questions.alt: Leave it as bare timber and oil it instead.
questions.alt2: Paint it, but a colour you choose from three sample pots first.

about: A made-up example. The shed has no window, so it is dark inside.
A window can go in one of two walls:
The south wall. More light, and it faces the house.
The east wall. Morning light only, and it faces the fence.
Cutting the opening is the same work either way.
questions.q: Do you want a window added on the south wall?
questions.yes: A window goes in the south wall.
questions.alt: Put the window in the east wall, facing the fence.
questions.alt2: No window. A skylight in the roof instead.

about: A made-up example. There is room for shelves along the back wall.
Three shelves would hold the paint tins and the seed trays. They would take about a hand's width off the floor space.
questions.q: Do you want three shelves on the back wall?
questions.yes: Three shelves go up on the back wall.
questions.alt: No shelves. Hooks on the back wall instead, so the floor stays clear.
